case_title: Om Prakash v. Union of India & Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304 Part II rlw s.34
confession: Voluntary confession recorded under Rule 23 of the Army Rules, 1954
aggravating_circumstances: Indulged in altercation, in a drunken state, alone in the room, escaped by rear door, absence at 'fall in parade'
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 304 Part II of IPC, sentenced to 7 years rigorous imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II of IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, an army officer, was involved in an altercation during a farewell party. The deceased attempted to intervene and was abused by the accused. After the party, the deceased was found in a pool of blood in his room. The accused was present in the room and was found lying on his bed. The deceased was taken to the hospital and declared dead. The accused surrendered at the police station and confessed to stabbing the deceased with a knife. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including witness testimonies and a medical report indicating the stab wound caused the death. The accused was alone in the room, and his absence from the 'fall in parade' and presence at the police station were considered against him. The trial court convicted him under Section 304 Part II of the IPC, and the conviction was upheld by the Armed Forces Tribunal and the Supreme Court.
